text.value: Most coaches, authors and influencers who tried ads got a pile of names, chased a few of them, gave up, and decided ads do not work for what they sell. Ads work fine. props.intro: Paid Ads = Booked Appointments is one of six systems we build. They are designed to connect, so nobody who raises a hand gets dropped between them.

props.text: We put booked sales calls on your calendar.

That is the only thing we are trying to fill: a day of calls with people who want what you teach, chose a time, and expect you to show up. Not names to chase. Not clicks. Booked calls, on the calendar you already use. Here is why my team and I are so stubborn about that. We are a modern day talent agency, and a talent agency's job was never just to get you noticed. It was to get you booked. Everything else on this page exists to produce that one thing, and a list of names does not come close to it.

text.label: Text: A list of names.
text.value: A list of names.

text.label: Text: This is what most people get when they pay for advertising.
text.value: This is what most people get when they pay for advertising. A sheet of names, phone numbers and email addresses. It looks like progress. But a name is only a person who was curious for one moment, and that moment is usually over by the time you see the list. Now the work lands on you. You call, you text, you hear nothing, you try again next week. You paid for the names, and then you paid again with your own evenings trying to turn them into something.

text.label: Text: A booked call.
text.value: A booked call.

text.label: Text: A booked call is a different animal. This person saw you, as
text.value: A booked call is a different animal. This person saw you, asked a question and got an answer right away. They asked another one and got that answered too. Then they looked at your calendar and picked a time. They know who you are and what you teach. They have been on your website. Some of them have already bought your e-book or listened to an episode of your podcast. By the time you say hello, the hardest part of the sale is behind you.

text.label: Text: Why it matters for you.
text.value: Why it matters for you.

text.label: Text: You sell something that takes a conversation. Nobody hands r
text.value: You sell something that takes a conversation. Nobody hands real money for a program to a stranger they saw in an ad five minutes ago. They want to talk to you, or to somebody on your team, and decide if you are the right person to help them. So the conversation is the only thing worth counting. A click is a step toward it. A form is a step toward it. Neither one is the thing itself, and neither one has ever paid a bill.

text.label: Text: What you do.
text.value: What you do.

text.label: Text: Your part is small on purpose. You show up to the call and t
text.value: Your part is small on purpose. You show up to the call and talk to somebody who wants help about whether what you teach is right for them. That is the work you are already good at. Everything that happens before that moment is done for you: the ad, the answer, the follow-up, the reminders, the booking. AI employees do it day and night, with my team behind them and me on your account.

text.label: Text: What your week looks like.
text.value: What your week looks like.

text.label: Text: You open your calendar on Monday and the calls are already t
text.value: You open your calendar on Monday and the calls are already there, each one with a name on it. There is no list to work through and no guilt about the messages you never got to. The people who did not book are not lost either. They are still being talked to, and they will keep hearing from you until they are ready or they tell us no. You stop being the person who chases, and go back to being the person who teaches.

text.value: The Facebook and Google ad accounts, the piece of code on your website that tells Facebook and Google which ads actually turned into buyers, and the calendar are yours and stay yours. What we add is the part those platforms do not do on their own: campaigns built around what one student or client is actually worth to you, and an answer to every person the moment they raise a hand. If we ever part ways, you keep all of it and nothing switches off.

Sending more people to a website that does not sell just loses money faster, so if the follow-up is slow or the website is not turning visitors into buyers, you will hear that from us before you hear it from your bank.

text.label: Heading: What goes wrong when the ads come first.
text.value: What goes wrong when the ads come first.

text.label: Text: The usual story.
text.value: The usual story.

text.label: Text: Somebody tells you ads are how you grow. So you hire a perso
text.value: Somebody tells you ads are how you grow. So you hire a person to run them, or you try it yourself on a weekend. Money starts going out on the first day. People click. A few fill out a form. A month later you have a bill, a short list of names, and almost nothing to show for it. If that has happened to you, it was not bad luck and it was not you. It was the order things were done in.

text.label: Text: Nowhere to land.
text.value: Nowhere to land.

text.label: Text: An ad has to send a person somewhere. If it sends them to a
text.value: An ad has to send a person somewhere. If it sends them to a social page, or to a website that does not explain who you are and what you sell, they look for a few seconds and leave. You paid for that visit whether they stayed or not. This is why the website is system one. Until there is a place you own that tells your story and gives a person something to buy or a call to book, an ad is just a paid trip to a locked door.

text.label: Text: Nobody answering.
text.value: Nobody answering.

text.label: Text: People do not ask questions on your schedule. They ask late
text.value: People do not ask questions on your schedule. They ask late at night, on a Sunday, or while you are on a call with a client. Their interest is at its highest the moment they ask. If the answer comes the next morning, they have already moved on, and often they have already bought from somebody who answered first. The ad platform charged you for that person just the same. Advertising with nobody answering is the most expensive way there is to help your competition.

text.label: Text: No proof.
text.value: No proof.

text.label: Text: A stranger who comes in from an ad has never heard of you. T
text.value: A stranger who comes in from an ad has never heard of you. The first thing they do is look for a sign that you have helped somebody like them. If they cannot find words from real clients, students or readers, they hesitate, and a person who hesitates online is gone. Your followers already trust you. People from an ad do not, and they will not take your word for it. They need to hear it from the people you have already helped.

text.label: Text: No second chance.
text.value: No second chance.

text.label: Text: Almost nobody is ready the first day. People need to see you
text.value: Almost nobody is ready the first day. People need to see you and hear from you seven to ten times before they trust you enough to pay. If nothing is following up with the ones who said not yet, every not yet turns into a never. You paid full price to meet that person and you got one try. Run ads that way and you are throwing away most of what you bought before it ever had a chance to pay you back.

text.label: Text: The wrong conclusion.
text.value: The wrong conclusion.

text.label: Text: So you decide ads do not work for what you sell. That is the
text.value: So you decide ads do not work for what you sell. That is the part that costs you the most, because it is not true. The ads did their job. They brought people. Everything that was supposed to be standing behind them was missing. Turning the water up does nothing for a bucket with holes in it. That is the whole reason this is system six and not system one. We fix the bucket first, on free attention, and only then turn up the water.

props.text: What this looked like on a real account.

Riverbend Wellness & Longevity, a health and wellness clinic in San Antonio. The ads were the last thing we turned on — instant follow-up went in first, connected to the calendar, with every inquiry recorded before anyone tried to act on it. Then the traffic started.

props.body: Booked on the calendar, not inquiries. The ads brought the people in and the instant follow-up turned them into appointments — every one of them answered in seconds, day or night.
props.heading: 28 appointments in a single month

props.body: Because the follow-up never stopped. Almost nobody gets paid on week-five leads, for the simple reason that almost nobody is still talking to them.
props.heading: A week-five lead cost the same as week one

props.body: So we could prove which appointments the system produced and which the front desk booked. Most reporting cannot separate the two.
props.heading: Every booking tagged to its source

props.text: Five weeks in, the system was still holding conversations with people who inquired in week one. Nobody shows you that part, and it is the part that made the numbers hold up.
Why we turn the ads on last.

Most agencies sell you traffic on day one, because traffic is the easy part to sell and the easy part to show. But traffic arriving at a page that cannot answer it is money poured on the floor. We put the answering in place first and get your free attention selling. Then we buy more attention, and what lands on your calendar is a booked call, not a list for somebody to work through. Think about what that order does for you. Not long ago you had to pay radio or TV just to be seen at all, so every lesson cost you money. Today your self-promotion starts on platforms that cost you nothing, so that is where we find out what people respond to, what they ask, and what makes them book. Every mistake gets made and fixed there, before a dollar of your ad money is at risk. By the time the ads go on, you are not testing whether this works. You are sending more people into something that already does.

Because the spend is yours, you can check that arithmetic yourself, any day of the week. If you have never run a business on these numbers, do not let the letters scare you. It is the same question a restaurant asks about a table or a roofer asks about a job: what did it cost me to get this customer, and what do they pay me over time? We work both numbers out with you in plain English before anything gets turned on, and we go over them with you every week after that. You will never have to take our word that the ads are working. You will be able to see it.
